title: Odometer Reading Used for Returned Kestrel Advantage Balloon Vehicles
content:
**Odometer statement standard.** For the excess mileage charge on a returned Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract, two odometer readings exist: the odometer the dealer recorded when signing the vehicle in on the return date (the contract's return odometer, which is the signed odometer statement) and the odometer recorded by the return inspection. Where more than one return inspection is on file the one with the latest inspection date is used, and of two dated the same day the one recorded first.

The miles driven are measured from:

- **the lower of the two readings**, where the dealer's sign-in odometer and the inspection odometer differ by at least one mile and by no more than 100 miles;
- **the dealer's sign-in odometer**, the signed odometer statement, where the two readings differ by more than 100 miles;
- **the inspection odometer**, where the two readings agree.

The difference is the absolute gap between the two readings, whichever is higher.

## Reading table (hypothetical readings)

| Sign-in odometer | Inspection odometer | Gap | Reading the miles driven are measured from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 41,000 | 41,000 | 0 | Inspection odometer, 41,000 |
| 41,000 | 41,001 | 1 | Lower reading, 41,000 |
| 41,100 | 41,000 | 100 | Lower reading, 41,000 |
| 41,000 | 41,101 | 101 | Sign-in odometer, 41,000 |
| 41,250 | 41,000 | 250 | Sign-in odometer, 41,250 |

## Basis questions

- **Which reading counts at a gap of exactly 100 miles?** The lower one; 100 is within the band of one to 100 miles.
- **Does the direction of the gap matter?** No; the gap is measured either way, and above 100 miles the sign-in reading is used whether it is the higher or the lower.
